findings:
🔵 [sweep-terminal-ignores-lease] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The sweep reaps `terminal` seat subtrees regardless of the worktree-lock signal, while the spec phrasing "terminal or unknown AND has no live lease" reads as lease-gating both. Excluded: a journaled terminal campaign has no resume reader, so a concurrent rail cannot be depending on its seats; the deviation only widens the safe (dead-artifact) case. If strict spec parity is wanted, add `r.lock_held_elsewhere` to the terminal branch's keep condition.
🔵 [rotation-suffix-assumption] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `campaignLastEvents` assumes rotated journals are `<ledger>.1..4` with `.1` newest; if the engine rotates with a different suffix scheme or keeps more generations, those events are invisible. Excluded as not a MUST-FIX: the engine path then reports `campaign_not_terminal:unjournaled` and keeps (fail-safe), and the sweep's `unknown`-with-no-lease reap is exactly the behaviour the spec mandates. Follow-up: assert the suffix scheme against the ledger writer's rotation code in a test.
🔵 [after-summary-omits-seats] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `report.after` recounts worktrees/branches but not `final_panel_seats`; actions already list removals, so nothing is silent. Cosmetic parity only.
🔵 [terminal-set-vs-abandoned] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES` is `terminal_ready|terminal_follow_up|terminal_stop`; if an "abandoned" campaign is journaled under a distinct event type, its seats are kept rather than reaped (safe direction, but less cleanup than the spec intends). Verify the event vocabulary in a follow-up; no resumable campaign can be deleted by this set.
